audience: From the Confirmations lead, to the owner of the on-line EnTelligence project / risk-system reporting, cc the head of Risk Management (to whom the desk heads report)
title: Request: read-only back-dated MTM report by counterparty for auditor requests
body:
Subject: Request: read-only back-dated MTM report by counterparty (would save Risk about 20 hours a month)

Hi,

**What I'm asking:** Please give Confirmations a read-only report that values all of a counterparty's deals across every desk as of a past date. It could be the on-line EnTelligence we planned or a standard report from the risk system, whichever is faster. Please reply by [date] with:
1. who will own it, and
2. a target date.

**Why:** Counterparties' auditors ask us for third-party MTM valuations several times a week. We have no system that values deals, so every request goes to all 5 or 6 Risk desk heads. Each desk then has an analyst pull a mini-book, export it to Excel, black out Delta/Vol and send it back. We estimate this costs about 92 minutes per request, or about 20 hours ($1,694) a month. Most of that time is spent by Risk staff. With this report, desk heads and analysts would no longer be involved.

**What the report needs to do:**
- Inputs: the counterparty short name and an as-of date (for example, Dec 29, 2000).
- Uses the curves as of that past date, which means back-dated curves have to be stored.
- Covers all desks and regions in one run, with no request to each desk.
- Output: MTM value and open position for each deal, plus a total. This should export to Excel so we can send it to the auditor.
- Delta/Vol are left out of the report entirely, so no one has to black them out.
- Read-only access for Confirmations staff.

Thanks,
[Confirmations lead]

---

**Background, for anyone who needs it**

*How it works today*
1. An auditor's request reaches Confirmations.
2. Confirmations emails all Risk desk heads (6 on one recent request, 5 on others). For example: "Can you provide MTM values as of Dec 29, 2000, for the short name of CROSS TIMBERS."
3. Each desk head passes the request to an analyst. The analyst pulls a mini-book for that counterparty as of the date, exports it to Excel, blacks out Delta/Vol and replies with the total MTM for that desk's region.
4. Confirmations combines the replies from all the desks and sends the result to the auditor.

Until the report exists, we will keep sending requests to the desks this way.

*How it would work*
Confirmations enters the short name and as-of date, runs the report and sends the export to the auditor. There is no request to the desks and no blacking out.

*How we got the savings figure*
92 minutes per request × 13 requests a month = 19.93 hours = $1,694.05 a month. The 13 a month comes from the stated rate of about 3 requests a week. Our email shows fewer: 4 requests over Feb–Mar 2001, about 1.5 a month. At that lower rate the saving would be smaller, so it's worth confirming the volume with the desks.

*Suggested acceptance test*
Run the new report for requests the desks have already answered and compare the results with what they sent:
- CoEnergy Trading Company as of Dec 31, 2000
- Cross Timbers as of Dec 29, 2000
- The two counterparties requested on Mar 21, 2001 (Dec 29, 2000)

If the totals match the desk replies for each region, the report is ready to replace the manual process.
